description.text: Henry VII, born 28 January 1457 at Pembroke Castle, was the son of Edmund Tudor and Lady Margaret Beaufort, whose lineage linked him to the Plantagenet dynasty through both the Tudor and Beaufort families. His claim to the throne was strengthened by his descent from Edward III and by his marriage to Elizabeth of York, which united the warring Lancastrian and Yorkist houses.

After seizing the crown at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485, Henry established a stable Tudor dynasty, consolidating power through strategic marriages, legal reforms, and a cautious but effective fiscal policy that restored England’s finances and ended the Wars of the Roses.

curiosities.text: Henry’s Welsh ancestry was a key factor in rallying support for his campaign; he famously displayed the red dragon of Wales during his triumphal procession in London.
He was the first English monarch to commission a dry dock, establishing the world's oldest surviving one at Portsmouth in 1495 to modernise the navy.
Henry’s reign saw the introduction of the pound avoirdupois as a standard of weight, a measure that would later become part of the Imperial system.
